title: Scalar derived reconstruction on disjoint closed rank supports
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion], and choose $D(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $r:Z\to\mathbb N$ be locally constant. Write $Z_n=\{r=n\}$ using [def-sc-locally-ranked-exterior-complex], with inclusion $j_n:Z_n\to Z$. For every $n\geq0$ let $E_n$ be an arbitrary module sheaf on $Z_n$. Set $T^q=j_{q,*}E_q$ for $q\geq0$ and $T^q=0$ for $q<0$, and let $C$ be the zero-differential complex with these terms. For any $K\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ with $H^q(K)\cong i_*T^q$ as scalar module sheaves for all $q\in\mathbb Z$, there is an isomorphism $K\cong Q(i_*C)$, where direct image is applied termwise. No finite-image assumption on r, no regularity assumption on i, and no action of $i_*\mathcal O_Z$ on K is required.

proof.text: For each integer n, invert the given degree-n homology isomorphism and apply the one-stratum scalar homology lift. Its lifting equation identifies the homology of the resulting single-degree map with an isomorphism, so that homology map is invertible.

Put P=i_*C and L_n=P^n[-n]. Each differential of P vanishes by additivity of pushforward. Construct the chain inclusions L_n to P by the identity on their degree-n term. The homology of this inclusion in degree n is invertible by the zero-differential short-complex calculation. Index the family by ULift of the integers to match the universe of module-sheaf coproducts. The termwise coproduct gives a derived coproduct, so the lifted maps assemble to a morphism g:Q(coproduct L_n) to K. The inclusions assemble to a chain morphism whose localization is a:Q(coproduct L_n) to Q(P).

Homology of the termwise coproduct is the coproduct of the homologies. In degree n all single-complex summands except n are zero; the n-th coprojection is invertible, with inverse obtained by the coproduct universal property. Thus the homology of the derived n-th coprojection is invertible. Its composite with H^n(a) is the single-term inclusion map, and its composite with H^n(g) is the chosen lift. Both are invertible, so H^n(a) and H^n(g) are invertible for every integer n. Homology detects derived isomorphisms. Compose the inverse of a with g and reverse the isomorphism to obtain K isomorphic to Q(P). All assembly and homology-detection glue is proved in the item module.
